renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: cnvkit_profile
  title: Copy-number profile
  description: |-
    Each dot is a genomic bin: its log2 copy ratio against the reference along the chromosomes, with the called segments drawn over the bins and coloured by their integer copy number, and the B-allele frequency of each segment underneath when it is known. It answers which regions of the genome are gained or lost in a sample.
    How to read: a log2 ratio near zero is a neutral, two-copy region. Segments above the gain line are gains and segments below the loss line are losses, and a deep drop is a possible homozygous deletion. Bins scattered widely around a segment mean a noisy sample, so check the bin depth card before trusting small segments.
    Lines and annotations: the gain line at a log2 ratio of 0.2 and the loss line at -0.25 are the inner cut-offs of the default thresholds of cnvkit call, chosen to detect a single-copy change in a diploid tumour at a purity as low as 30%. They assume a diploid genome and are rescaled by purity when it is given.
    Sources: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/pipeline.html and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27100738/
  kind: cnv_profile
  config:
    gain_threshold: 0.2
    loss_threshold: -0.25
    y_range: 3.0
  roles:
    sample: sample
    chrom: chrom
    start: start
    end: end
    log2: log2
    baf: baf
    copy_number: copy_number
    segment: segment
    label: label

- component: card
  id: cnvkit_log2_spread
  title: Copy-ratio spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of the bin-level log2 copy ratios, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how far the bins stray from a neutral ratio.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a few extreme bins means a mostly neutral genome with a few alterations. A wide box means a noisy sample or many copy-number changes. The range is shown instead of a median, because gains and losses cancel to about zero.
    Lines and annotations: bins are the rows of the copy ratio file, one per genomic bin, with segments left out.
    Source: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/fileformats.html
  column: log2
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('segment') == 'bin'
  caption: bin log2 ratio, with its spread

- component: card
  id: cnvkit_bin_depth
  title: Bin depth
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median read depth of the bins, with the quartiles beside it and the histogram of the depths below. It answers whether the sample is covered deeply enough for reliable calls.
    How to read: a narrow histogram of depths means even coverage. CNVkit documentation notes that larger alterations are called reliably down to about 10x on-target coverage, with more spurious segments below that. A long tail of low-depth bins is noisy.
    Lines and annotations: the 10x figure in the documentation concerns on-target coverage, and no line is drawn for it here.
    Source: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/pipeline.html
  column: depth
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - q1
  - q3
  secondary_layout: histogram
  filter_expr: col('segment') == 'bin'
  caption: bin depth, with its distribution

- component: table
  title: Bins and segments table
  description: |-
    Each row is a bin or a called segment with its position, log2 copy ratio, integer copy number and the gene label CNVkit gives it. It answers the exact values behind the profile.
    How to read: filter the segment column to segments to list the calls, then sort by log2 to find the strongest gains and losses.
    Source: https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/fileformats.html and https://cnvkit.readthedocs.io/en/stable/pipeline.html
  columns:
  - sample
  - chrom
  - start
  - end
  - log2
  - copy_number
  - segment
  - label
